paper.title: MiraBench: Evaluating Action-Conditioned Reliability in Robotic World Models

claim: Robotic world-model evaluation should move beyond visual fidelity toward action-conditioned reliability, including physical adherence, action-following fidelity, and optimism-bias detection.

evidence.summary: The paper frames existing evaluations as weak evidence for whether action-conditioned predictions are reliable, then defines MiraBench around physics adherence, action fidelity, and failure-case optimism bias.
evidence.locator: Abstract; Problem Formulation; Design of MIRABENCH

notes: HTML extraction available; this event summarizes the paper's own benchmark framing.

paper.title: RoboTrustBench: Benchmarking the Trustworthiness of Video World Models for Robotic Manipulation

claim: Trustworthy robotic video world-model evaluation needs constraint-sensitive, counterfactual, and adversarial scenarios because visual coherence and surface instruction following do not establish robotic trustworthiness.

evidence.summary: RoboTrustBench evaluates video world models with four scenario types and a six-dimensional protocol, reporting failures in constraint reasoning, counterfactual grounding, physical interaction, and unsafe-instruction suppression.
evidence.locator: Abstract; Evaluation Dimensions; Analysis of Trustworthiness Failures

notes: HTML extraction available; event is based on abstract and evaluation-section matches.

paper.title: τ0-WM: A Unified Video-Action World Model for Robotic Manipulation

claim: A video-action world model can support pre-execution action evaluation by imagining candidate futures, scoring task progress, and rectifying low-quality action candidates.

evidence.summary: The paper presents a unified video-action world model that combines policy learning, video prediction, and action evaluation, using test-time sampling, ranking, and simulator-based rectification before execution.

paper.title: VLM-DEWM: Dynamic External World Model for Verifiable and Resilient Vision-Language Planning in Manufacturing

institutions.name: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

claim: For dynamic manufacturing, an external queryable world model can make VLM planning more verifiable by separating persistent state management from semantic reasoning and checking decisions before execution.

evidence.summary: VLM-DEWM validates each VLM decision against a persistent world model and uses discrepancy analysis for targeted recovery, with reported gains in state tracking and recovery success in long-horizon manufacturing tasks.

notes: The claim is conditional on the semi-structured manufacturing setting studied by the paper.

paper.title: VLM-DEWM: Dynamic External World Model for Verifiable and Resilient Vision-Language Planning in Manufacturing

institutions.name: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

claim: External world-model verification has explicit deployment boundaries: corrupted perception can pollute the world model, closed-world assumptions fail on novel objects, and geometry-only checks do not verify dynamics or kinematics.

evidence.summary: The limitations section identifies upstream perception errors, open-vocabulary failures under closed-world assumptions, and a dynamics gap in the physical verification scope.
evidence.locator: 4.4.2 Limitations and Failure Mode Analysis; Scope of Physical Verification (Dynamics Gap)

notes: This event is a boundary condition rather than a general rejection of the approach.
